scope.content_policy: One fictional client and one fictional event are used throughout. All names, venues, vendors, times, ticket codes, maps and accessibility details are demo content, not claims about a real event.

client.name: Morrow Harbor Night Market & River Arts Festival
client.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
client.description: An invented one-evening community event combining independent food, small-batch makers, riverside performances and free public workshops in the fictional Bellwether District.
client.promise: An evening made by the river, for everyone.
client.demo_notice: Fictional event concept. No tickets, bookings or real locations are represented.

planned_design_system.rationale: A lantern-led wayfinding family: warm human invitation at a distance, strict utility structure at close range.

type.display: Noto Sans CJK SC, bold, tight uppercase or short Chinese display lines
type.numerals: DejaVu Sans Mono, for times, zones and ticket codes

geometry.lantern_motif: A shared DSL-built semicircular lantern window with three vertical mullions; permitted to crop or simplify at small sizes.
geometry.river_line: Two offset horizontal curves expressed as stepped DSL bands or bounded path shapes; a secondary connector, not a required background on every item.
geometry.corner_radius: 0 for large outdoor signs; 16-24 px for cards and badges

layout.outdoor_scale: Display title at least 10 percent of image width; body scale by actual viewing distance.
layout.portable_scale: Single-column reading on badge/card; explicit hierarchy rather than shrinking the poster.
layout.information_rule: English and simplified Chinese may alternate by touchpoint, but names, date, hours, location and zone codes must never change.

shared_documentation.role: Tags, layouts, clipping, image and decoration syntax
Font, line, wrap, inline span and baseline rules
Adapting components across aspect ratios and viewing distances

cases.title: Festival teaser poster
cases.audience: District residents and cultural visitors deciding whether to attend
cases.use_context: Portrait street poster outside a fictional arts centre, read at 2-5 metres before the full programme exists
cases.user_goal: Remember the event name and date, grasp its food/music/making mix and know where to learn more

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Morrow Harbor fictional identity, event promise, date, hours and location; three invented programme highlights and a non-live demo information line.

cases.visual_intent: A monumental lantern window rises over layered river bands; bold event typography sits in the light while three concise programme cues anchor the lower third.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Event name, 18 October 2027, 16:00-22:00 and North Quay are readable and exactly match the shared brief.
completion_criteria.check_method: Full-size and thumbnail review plus cross-case copy comparison.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Food, music and making are all apparent in a thumbnail without requiring body copy.
completion_criteria.check_method: 480 px-wide thumbnail inspection and label inventory.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Lantern motif and river bands form a recognisable family device without obscuring type or clipping at the canvas edge.
The fictional-event demo notice is present and readable.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: The awareness-stage poster solves attraction at long distance; no transaction, route, timetable or staff procedure is embedded beyond three programme cues.

cases.title: Quayside hanging banner
cases.audience: People approaching the fictional North Quay from the district's main walking route
cases.use_context: Tall double-sided street banner concept viewed obliquely at 8-20 metres, with wind and distance reducing fine-detail visibility
cases.user_goal: Recognise the festival, confirm the walking direction and read the event date without stopping

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Shared fictional festival identity, invented route-direction arrow, date and North Quay destination. No real traffic direction is asserted.

cases.visual_intent: Exploit the vertical format: split Morrow / HARBOR into stacked letters, anchor a large directional lantern arrow and keep only date and destination as support copy.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Festival name, date and North Quay remain identifiable in a 180 px-wide thumbnail.
completion_criteria.check_method: Extreme downscale inspection at intended aspect ratio.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The directional arrow is a single unmistakable form and is labelled as fictional demo wayfinding.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect arrow silhouette and its caption.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: All critical content stays clear of a planned 40 px banner safe zone and mounting exclusion band.
The banner shares the poster's palette, type character and lantern language while adapting the composition vertically.
completion_criteria.check_method: Side-by-side family review after both render.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A distance-led navigation banner has a distinct narrow ratio, oblique viewing and minimal message; it is not a resized teaser poster.

cases.title: River Pass admission ticket
cases.audience: Ticketed attendees arriving at the fictional gate and keeping the pass for re-entry
cases.use_context: Printed landscape ticket held in the hand at the entrance, then folded or shown to stewards
cases.user_goal: Confirm admission type, date and entry rule, find the gate and present the correct demo code

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented River Pass ticket MH-DEMO-018, fictional one-day general admission, gate Q, date and re-entry rule. The code is decorative and deliberately non-scannable.

cases.visual_intent: Use a horizontal ticket with a detachable-looking stub, large gate letter, monospaced code and compact event identity; move away from poster scale into hand-held precision.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Ticket type, date, event hours, gate Q, demo code and re-entry rule are complete and readable at hand-held size.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect at 100% and at 600 px-wide equivalent.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Stub separation and code association are clear; no decorative line crosses text.
The code is labelled demo/non-scannable and the footer says fictional event.
completion_criteria.check_method: Read labels and inspect that no real barcode is claimed.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Shared date, location and naming match the poster and banner exactly.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A transactional admission object has to work in the hand, carry a unique demo code and show an entry rule; its compact landscape structure is functionally separate from awareness media.

cases.title: North Quay festival site map
cases.audience: Arriving attendees, families and access-conscious visitors planning their route
cases.use_context: Printed A2 map at the fictional entry plaza and reproduced on a nearby interpretation panel; read standing at 0.5-1.5 metres
cases.user_goal: Locate entrance, four zones, toilets, water, first aid and the step-free route before moving through the site

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented schematic North Quay site with four zones A-D, three fictional gates and demo amenity locations; not based on a real map and not to scale.

cases.visual_intent: A simplified river-edge plan uses the shared river line as a boundary, lantern pins for zones and a heavier dashed step-free path; labels and symbols carry meaning independently of colour.
dsl_capabilities: dashed-style path segments built from DSL

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Zones A-D, three gates, toilets, water, first aid, information and step-free route are all shown with matching legend entries.
completion_criteria.check_method: Map-to-legend inventory and visual inspection of every symbol.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The map states fictional concept and not to scale; the route is not presented as verified accessible terrain.
No label covers a route junction, pin or neighbouring zone, and the river boundary reads consistently.
completion_criteria.check_method: 100% overlap review and trace the step-free path end to end.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Zone letters and amenity symbols remain distinguishable in grayscale.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: The only spatial-navigation touchpoint; it must represent relationships between places and amenities rather than simply restate event identity or a schedule.

cases.title: River Stage running-order screen
cases.audience: Audience members at the fictional River Stage checking what is happening next
cases.use_context: Widescreen stage-side display and lobby mirror, read at 3-12 metres during a continuously changing event represented by one planned static frame
cases.user_goal: Identify the current act, next performance, start time and any stage status change

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented River Stage running order with fictional performers, current 19:10 slot, next 19:40 slot and demo status labels; no live schedule connection.

cases.visual_intent: Make NOW and NEXT the dominant split, use a large lantern clock-like marker and keep the full event identity small; recede secondary programme details into a bottom rail.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Current and next performer names and times are readable in a 480 px-wide thumbnail with no ambiguity.
completion_criteria.check_method: Extreme downscale review and temporal hierarchy check.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: A visible static-demo label prevents the frame being mistaken for a live schedule.
NOW and NEXT use both words and layout position, not colour alone.
Footer details use smaller supporting type without introducing unreadable clutter or conflicting times.
completion_criteria.check_method: 100% footer review and cross-case date/time check.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: This is a temporal, large-screen utility surface for an audience already on site; its NOW/NEXT hierarchy is structurally unlike the ticket, map and promotional banner.

cases.title: Made by the River tote
cases.audience: Attendees who want a reusable festival bag and visitors buying from fictional makers
cases.use_context: Cotton tote print concept seen folded on a stall, then carried through the site; one side shown as a complete print layout
cases.user_goal: Identify the event affiliation and discover the maker/food zones represented on the bag

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Shared Morrow Harbor identity with the invented phrase 'Made by the River' and fictional zones A and C. No merchandise is offered for sale by this concept.

cases.visual_intent: A bold single-colour-friendly lantern silhouette and two-line wordmark dominate the cloth; fine detail is reduced so the identity survives fabric texture, folds and distance.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Event name and lantern mark remain recognisable in a 240 px-wide thumbnail.
The design uses no essential detail finer than the planned 24 px print-safe stroke and stays inside the tote safe area.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect line widths and safe-zone bounds.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The palette remains legible in a one-colour simulation on a contrasting fabric colour.
completion_criteria.check_method: Temporary monochrome contrast review outside final outputs.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Small copy accurately names the fictional zones and does not claim real merchandise availability.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect lower copy and demo notice.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A carried textile object needs simplified recognition under folds and texture, not detailed instructions; it tests the design system's ability to lose detail gracefully.

cases.title: Lantern Court vendor counter card
cases.audience: Visitors browsing fictional food vendors in zone A
cases.use_context: Small landscape counter card in front of each stall, read at arm's length while a queue moves
cases.user_goal: Identify the vendor, understand one signature item, check dietary and price information and choose a payment queue

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented vendor 'Coal & Citron', three demo dishes, fictional prices, ingredient markers and fictional cashless-only policy. No real vendor or allergen claim is made.

cases.visual_intent: Keep a persistent lantern tab for the festival and zone A, then give the fictional vendor a compact price-board hierarchy with a large signature-item panel and clearly labelled markers.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Vendor name, zone A, three item names and prices, payment note and demo dietary labels are complete.
The signature item dominates, but price rows remain scannable and aligned.
completion_criteria.check_method: Thumbnail hierarchy review and row-alignment inspection.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Dietary information is explicitly fictional demo content and not presented as certified allergen advice.
Festival identity remains subordinate but recognisable and matches the site map's zone A name.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A vendor-level transactional card balances two identities and dense small print at close range; it is not another whole-event awareness piece or a screen schedule.

cases.title: Steward and volunteer badge
cases.audience: Fictional event stewards, volunteers and attendees seeking assistance
cases.use_context: Wearable badge seen across a busy entrance or aisle, often at 1-3 metres and at an angle
cases.user_goal: Identify the wearer's role and zone, distinguish stewards from general volunteers and know whether they can provide access assistance

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented badge for a zone C maker-hall steward with fictional volunteer name 'Lin R.', role labels and a demo access-assistance indicator.

cases.visual_intent: Use high-contrast role-first typography, a large zone letter and a clipped lantern badge shape; the festival wordmark is small enough to leave room for instant role recognition.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: STEWARD, zone C and the fictional name are identifiable in a 320 px-wide thumbnail.
Role, access-assistance indicator and general volunteer status cannot be confused; text labels accompany symbols.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect each role element and compare semantics to the brief.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: No text enters the planned clip or mounting exclusion area and no corners cut through glyphs.
Zone C matches the site map and the fictional demo badge notice is present.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A wearable staff credential has a unique role-recognition task and physical clipping constraints; it is not a customer ticket or public sign.

cases.title: Quiet Deck access guide card
cases.audience: Visitors seeking step-free routes, quieter spaces, seating or assistance
cases.use_context: A5 double-sided-style guide represented in one landscape proof, handed to visitors at the fictional information point
cases.user_goal: Find the step-free route to zone D, understand available quiet-space etiquette and locate fictional assistance contacts

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Invented guide describing a schematic step-free route, a fictional quiet deck, seating, assistance point and demo etiquette. It does not certify real accessibility.

cases.visual_intent: Calm the festival palette into a mist/ink card, use a simple three-stop route diagram and pair each practical note with a large labelled symbol; keep the lantern mark as a small continuity cue.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Three schematic stops, zone D, quiet-space etiquette, seating, assistance point and demo contact are complete and readable.
The card explicitly says the route and facilities are fictional demo content and not a real accessibility audit.
Every symbol has a text label and remains understandable in grayscale.
Route stop names and zone D exactly match the site map.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A personal, close-reading access guide serves visitors with specific information needs; it adapts the same identity through reduced visual stimulation and practical route content.

cases.title: Afterglow thank-you poster
cases.audience: Attendees, volunteers, vendors and district partners after the fictional event
cases.use_context: Portrait poster at the fictional organiser's studio and partner noticeboards, read after the event rather than during arrival
cases.user_goal: Recognise a shared thank-you message, see the event's four community contributions and know the demo next-step for staying involved

content_basis.label: FICTIONAL_DEMO
content_basis.description: Fictional post-event thank-you with invented aggregate attendance and four invented community contributions; clearly labelled as illustrative demo figures, not measured results.

cases.visual_intent: Turn the lantern motif inside out into a radiant closing mark, use a warm paper field and a four-part contribution grid; preserve the family while shifting from urgency to reflection.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: Thank-you message, organiser, four contribution statements and fictional next-step are present and legible.
Any attendance or participation figures are visibly labelled illustrative demo figures and are not presented as verified outcomes.
completion_criteria.check_method: Inspect every metric label and footer.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: The closing lantern echoes the teaser but its reflective composition does not simply recolour or reuse the teaser layout.
completion_criteria.check_method: Compare structure and focal hierarchy side by side.

completion_criteria.observable_condition: No text or contribution panel is clipped and the lower demo footer remains readable.

criteria_history.reason: Initial criteria fixed before the first Snapshot render request.

cases.independence_rationale: A post-event accountability/thank-you piece addresses reflection and future participation; its four contribution statements and closing motif differ from pre-event promotion and on-site operations.
